newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait Stock Exchange tops record highs in week.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait Stock Exchange tops record highs in week.

text.p: Volume, value and index hit new peaks in the week to Wednesday on Kuwait's bourse with capital flows from neighbouring Gulf states fueling already active trade, dealers said.
The index, making the third record high in as many weeks, rose 73.5 points, or 4.1 percent, to 1,855.7 points.

"Due to lack of other investment openings in Kuwait and the region and strong market indicators, capital started flowing in from abroad," said dealer Mohammad al-Duhaishi. "The market is in a position to become a regional market."

Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest through mutual funds ran by local firms.
Kuwait is considering opening trade to foreign investors.
Traded value rose 60 percent to 358.7 million dinars ($1.2 billion), a daily average of 71.7 million dinars. The exchange operates for two and a half hours five days a week.
Volume gained 53.3 percent to 1.625 billion shares, a daily average of 325 million. Gainers led losers 32-14 in the week, while nine were non-movers.
"There are economic factors that encourage the positive development in the market such as good mid-year results by (listed) firms," economist Ammer al-Tamimi said.
Dealers said a high-tech trading system installed last year often breaks due to excessive trading.
"They (market officials) said they will extend the capacity of the system soon," one dealer said. "Trade could have been even more active had there been no break downs."

Kuwait Cement Company shares rose 8.4 percent to 450 fils on news that the firm plans to build a clinker plant with a capacity of one million tonnes per year expandable to two million in later stages.
Kuwait Real Estate Bank rose 15 percent to 415 fils following reports that the state will shed most of its 32.9 percent stake in the bank in a privatisation bid.
Commercial Bank, Bahrain International Bank, Investment Projects, Pearl of Kuwait Real Estate, Coast Development, United Realty and Fujairah Cement were among the most traded shares.

Banks were the most active sector by value with 31 percent, investment shares followed with 30 percent and foreign firms with 16 percent. Investment firms were the most active by volume with 32.5 percent.
